name: Randall Fryer

bio.statement: In his voters' pamphlet statement, Fryer lists his occupation as retired physician, with a background in rural emergency medicine, family practice and software.
bio.excerpt: Occupation: Physician, retired. Occupational Background: Emergency medicine at several rural Oregon hospitals (locum). Family Practice Medicine. Product software integration manager, technical marketing support, software developer.

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Washington County edition), p. 49

bio.statement: Fryer lists a Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine from Western University of Health Sciences and a Bachelor of Liberal Arts from St. John's College.
bio.excerpt: Educational Background: Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine, College of Osteopathic Medicine of the Pacific, Western University of Health Sciences. Bachelor of Liberal Arts, St. John's College, Santa Fe, NM.

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Washington County edition), p. 49

bio.statement: Fryer lists combat medic service in the U.S. Army as his prior governmental experience.
bio.excerpt: Prior Governmental Experience: Combat Medic, United States Army

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Washington County edition), p. 49

positions.statement: Fryer says he would reduce administrative growth, free teachers from state mandates and set high graduation standards.
positions.excerpt: Prune bloated administrative growth and free good teachers from one-size-fits-all mandates from Salem. Set high standards for graduation, and students will rise to meet them.

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Washington County edition), p. 49

positions.statement: Fryer says sobriety centers and detox should be required for people cycling through the streets.
positions.excerpt: Sobriety centers and detox should be required, not optional, for those cycling through our streets.

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Washington County edition), p. 49

positions.statement: Fryer says Salem keeps adding taxes, fees and regulations and that Oregon can downsize its government at the ballot box.
positions.excerpt: Oregon can downsize its government at the ballot box, or watch family out-migration and a shrinking private sector do it for us.

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Washington County edition), p. 49
